pluss::timeline::moment¶

Back to Timeline Factory API Reference

Signatures¶

Timeline pluss::timeline::moment(std::string_view expression,
                                 const MomentOptions& options = {})
Timeline pluss::timeline::moment(text_range expressions,
                                 const MomentOptions& options = {})
Timeline pluss::timeline::moment(nested_text expressions,
                                 const MomentOptions& options = {})

Resolve Text At The Moment Of The Call¶

moment() turns either ordinary datetime text or a deliberately small calendar expression into concrete epoch nanoseconds. The result stores the resolved instant, not the expression. Calling moment("today") now and retaining the returned scalar therefore preserves today’s boundary; it does not change when the value is read tomorrow.

Use make() when every input is datetime text. Use moment() when an input may instead name a boundary relative to the current clock, such as the start of the current month. now() and today() are shorter spellings for the two most common scalar expressions.

The expression vocabulary is intentionally finite:

Base

Resolved instant

now

the current system-clock instant

today

midnight at the start of the current calendar date

yesterday

midnight at the start of the preceding calendar date

tomorrow

midnight at the start of the following calendar date

start_of_month

midnight on day 1 of the current calendar month

end_of_month

midnight on the final day of the current calendar month

Names are ASCII case-insensitive and whitespace may surround or separate their parts. Each base may have one signed integer offset with unit s, m, h, d, or w, for example today + 6h, now-15m, or end_of_month - 1d. Offsets are fixed elapsed durations: 1d is exactly 24 hours and 1w is exactly seven such days. They are not month arithmetic or business-calendar rules.

Parsing Modes¶

MomentOptions::mode decides which language is accepted:

Mode

Accepted input

MomentMode::Auto

expressions and strict datetime text

MomentMode::ExpressionOnly

only the expression vocabulary above

MomentMode::Strict

only ordinary datetime text, with the same parsing contract as make()

Auto is useful at an interactive boundary that genuinely accepts both forms. Prefer Strict for persisted records and protocol input: accepting today there would make the same record mean different instants on different runs. Prefer ExpressionOnly for configuration fields that are explicitly rules, because a misspelled rule cannot silently become ordinary datetime input.

UTC And Local Calendar Boundaries¶

MomentOptions::clock affects calendar expressions, not absolute datetime text and not now. MomentClock::UTC resolves today, yesterday, tomorrow, and month boundaries at UTC midnight. MomentClock::Local first obtains the process-local calendar date and then resolves midnight in the process-local timezone, including the applicable daylight-saving offset.

The stored value is still an absolute instant. A local midnight can therefore display as a non-midnight UTC clock time until the Timeline is projected to the desired named timezone. This distinction matters: selecting the local date but attaching UTC midnight would describe a different instant, and moment() does not do that.

Example 1: Strict Parsing Preserves Nanoseconds¶

const auto fixed = pluss::timeline::moment(
    "2024-02-29T12:34:56.123456789Z",
    {pluss::timeline::MomentMode::Strict,
     pluss::timeline::MomentClock::UTC});

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::timeline::format(fixed, "%FT%T.%f%z")) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"2024-02-29T12:34:56.123456789+00:00"

Example 2: A Range Keeps Its Shape¶

const std::vector<std::string> text{
    "2024-01-01", "2024-06-30T23:59:59Z"};
const auto values = pluss::timeline::moment(
    text,
    {pluss::timeline::MomentMode::Strict,
     pluss::timeline::MomentClock::UTC});

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::timeline::format(values, "%FT%T.%f%z")) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["2024-01-01T00:00:00.000000000+00:00", "2024-06-30T23:59:59.000000000+00:00"]

Nested text preserves rectangular shape up to Timeline’s rank-three limit in the same way. Every lane is resolved during this call, so do not call moment() separately for lanes that must share one exact now; capture a scalar once and reuse it instead.

Example 3: Verify A Dynamic Boundary Without Inventing A Date¶

const auto today = pluss::timeline::moment(
    "today",
    {pluss::timeline::MomentMode::ExpressionOnly,
     pluss::timeline::MomentClock::UTC});
const auto plus_three_hours = pluss::timeline::moment(
    " TODAY + 3H ",
    {pluss::timeline::MomentMode::ExpressionOnly,
     pluss::timeline::MomentClock::UTC});

const auto exact_offset =
    plus_three_hours.epoch_nanos().item<std::int64_t>() -
    today.epoch_nanos().item<std::int64_t>();

std::cout << (today.hour().item<std::int32_t>() == 0) << '\n';
std::cout << (exact_offset == 3LL * 60 * 60 * 1'000'000'000) << '\n';

Output¶

true
true

This checks the contract while remaining correct on every day the example is run. Printing a hard-coded date for today would be false documentation.

Example 4: Calendar Words Describe Adjacent Boundaries¶

const auto options = pluss::timeline::MomentOptions{
    pluss::timeline::MomentMode::ExpressionOnly,
    pluss::timeline::MomentClock::UTC};

const auto yesterday = pluss::timeline::moment("yesterday", options);
const auto today = pluss::timeline::moment("today", options);
const auto tomorrow = pluss::timeline::moment("tomorrow", options);
const auto first = pluss::timeline::moment("start_of_month", options);
const auto last = pluss::timeline::moment("end_of_month", options);

const auto day_ns = 86'400LL * 1'000'000'000;
std::cout << (today.epoch_nanos().item<std::int64_t>() -
                  yesterday.epoch_nanos().item<std::int64_t>() == day_ns) << '\n';
std::cout << (tomorrow.epoch_nanos().item<std::int64_t>() -
                  today.epoch_nanos().item<std::int64_t>() == day_ns) << '\n';
std::cout << (first.day().item<std::int32_t>() == 1) << '\n';
std::cout << ((last + pluss::duration::days(1)).day().item<std::int32_t>() == 1)
          << '\n';

Output¶

true
true
true
true

Failures And Limits¶

moment() throws when an expression has an unknown base, more than one offset, a fractional or missing offset magnitude, an unknown unit, or an offset that exceeds the representable nanosecond range. Strict throws on an expression, while ExpressionOnly throws on ordinary datetime text. Invalid calendar text follows the same rejection rules as make().

The local clock mode depends on the process timezone and the host timezone database. Use UTC when reproducibility across machines is more important than the host’s civil calendar. Use a local expression only when process-local midnight is specifically the boundary you mean.

See Also¶

  • now: capture the current instant without expression text.

  • today: capture the start of the current UTC or local date.

  • make: parse datetime text without relative expressions.
